summary: GitHub sign-in: fresh refute-first review of U5 after its two fix rounds; one fix round if blocking, then a fresh re-review

findings.problem: The U5-R11 hold restart (src/main/github-signin.ts:351-356) honours a rate-limit or transient hold only in the clock's own time: a backward step re-anchors the hold at the new time, and the forward correction that usually follows (NTP, Windows Time after resume, a user fixing the clock) then lands past the re-anchored `until`, so a refresh goes out while GitHub's retry-after is still running (E-15 l.36, L-13, pre-mortem 4). The hold is shortened by (step size - time elapsed since it was set); for a step larger than the hold the correction cancels it outright. 8749974's message and the ARCHITECTURE line claim a backward step 'neither cancels it nor stretches it'; that holds for one step alone, not for a step and its correction, and the R11 pins (refresh test 6, U5-R11 cases; test 15) never move the clock forward again after the step.
findings.evidence: Scratch tests in a private copy of HEAD (scratchpad/u5rev3/wt2/tests/zz-u5-review3.test.ts; the worktree untouched, sha256 828c3b81...550b6 before and after). P-A: token past expiry, the refresh answered 429 retry-after 120 (GITHUB_RATE_LIMIT, 1 refresh request); clock back a day, a read is held; clock set to t0 + 10 s (real time 10 s into the 120 s window): the read refreshed and succeeded - output `P-A {"outcome":"200:signed-in","refreshes":2,...}`, assertion 'promise resolved "{ status: 200, authenticated: true }" instead of rejecting'. P-B: the same hold, a 30 s step back at t0 + 1 s, then the correction at t0 + 95 s (25 s of retry-after left): 'expected [ ...(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2' - a second refresh request inside the window. Both pass with holdActive in its R11 form only because no shipped test steps the clock forward after a backward step.
findings.fix: Give a hold a second anchor that a wall-clock step cannot move: a monotonic reading (performance.now(), injected as an optional `monotonic?()` dep beside now/sleep in GitHubSignInDeps, 3.7 is U5's own API) taken when the hold is set, and keep the hold active while EITHER now() < until OR monotonic() - monoSetAt < the hold's length. A system sleep can then over-hold by at most the hold's own length (<= 1 h), which is the bounded trade the fixer worried about, while no step pair can shorten it. Add P-A and P-B to refresh case 6 as pins (red on HEAD). If the lead prefers to keep the wall clock alone, record under 6.8 and Known limits that a backward step followed by a forward correction shortens a hold by the step, and correct 8749974's claim in As built.

perFinding.done: Fixed in d87f796 (S3, code change, red-first), with a disclosed departure from the finding's sketch. GitHubSignInDeps (3.7, U5's own API) gains `monotonic?(): number`, default `() => performance.now()`; a hold is `{ setAt: a monotonic reading, lengthMs, reason }`, set by one setHold() from renew()'s rate-limited branch and from failed(); holdActive() is `monotonic() - setAt < lengthMs`. The finding proposed keeping the U5-R11 restarted wall-clock anchor and OR-ing the monotonic one to it; the commit times the hold on the monotonic clock alone, because a disjunction can only extend the hold beyond its monotonic length, and its wall branch does so only after a backward step, by the real time elapsed before the step: an over-hold that protects nothing, while it would keep R11's restart write, the one impure write status() made (2.3). Mutation M13-or (the finding's OR form applied to the fixed code) ran 89 red 0: no test can reach that wall branch, the class U5-R14 retired. The system-sleep cost is the finding's own and identical in both forms (over-hold of at most the hold's length). Pins: a test.each of three under refresh case 6 (U5-R13): P-A (a day's step at 0 s into a 429/120 s hold, the correction at 10 s of real time), P-B (a 30 s step at 1 s, correction at 95 s) and a 500/30 s case (a 10 s step at 5 s, correction at 26 s); each read after the correction is still held with one refresh request, held at holdMs-1 of real time, refreshing at holdMs, 200 with the new token; after the day's step the clock calls the expired token valid, so it goes out once and its 401 refreshes nothing under the hold (GS-4, the 6.8 known limit, as test 15 models it). The test Clock gained a monotonic reading (`t` less a skew only `step(ms)` moves) and the harness injects it; the three R11 pins, test 15 and the 301 000 ms skew case now step with step() and the R11/15 titles say the hold runs on rather than restarts (assertions unchanged). ARCHITECTURE U5 line extended. For the lead (As built / 6.8): a hold is timed on a monotonic clock for its length of real time, superseding the 2.3 formula `now() < hold.until`, the R7 setAt and the R11 restart notes already owed; the 6.8 'System sleep' row may add the bounded over-hold; src/main/index.ts does not construct the service yet, so U6's wiring takes the default.

findings.problem: A successful refresh no longer resets the consecutive-error count `sameError`, so the account is cleared (ended: sign-in-ended, both vault entries gone) by ONE identical refresh error that follows a success, instead of three in a row. Spec 6.5 pseudo-code resets `sameError` for every answer that is not `error`/`unusable` BEFORE the kinds are dispatched, `tokens` included, and 6.5 'Clearing the hold' says `sameError` is cleared by a successful refresh; L-12 (2.4) allows a clear only for the same unknown `error` code, or the same `unusable` status (GS-2), maxSameRefreshError (3) times IN A ROW. On HEAD, renew() returns at the `tokens` branch (src/main/github-signin.ts:466, `return this.adopt(...)`) before the reset at :474, and adopt() (:494) resets `hold` and `failures` only. This is a regression from fix round 1: at 8e3ce77 the reset (line 441) ran before the whole switch including `case 'tokens'`; 968852e (U5-R10) hoisted the `tokens` branch above it, and R11-R14 kept that order. No shipped test covers an identical answer on either side of a successful refresh (the 'only consecutive identical answers count' pin at tests/github-signin-refresh.test.ts:338 puts a 500 between the errors, which still reaches :474), so the rule has no guard.

Both rows red: output `P-C {"outcome":"GITHUB_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED","refreshes":4,"status":{"state":"signed-out","ended":"sign-in-ended",...},"live":false}`, assertion "expected 'GITHUB_SIGN_IN_REQUIRED' to be 'GITHUB_RENEWAL_UNAVAILABLE'". findings.fix: Move `if (answer.kind !== 'error' && answer.kind !== 'unusable') this.sameError = null;` from src/main/github-signin.ts:474 to directly after the live-account check (:465) and before `if (answer.kind === 'tokens') return this.adopt(...)` (:466), i.e. the spec's 6.5 order, placed after the live check so a late answer about another account still counts and resets nothing (U5-R10/R12). Alternative: `this.sameError = null` beside `this.hold = null; this.failures = 0` in adopt() (:494), which resets only on an admitted persist; either satisfies the test. Add P-C's two rows as a red-first pin under refresh test 4 (red on HEAD with the message above; green with the move), record the guard proof (the moved line deleted: the new pin red; the existing :338 pin stays green only because its separator is a 500, so name both), and in the commit report say 968852e introduced the regression. Nothing is owed to As built beyond the 6.5 note already owed for R12/R14.

findings.problem: The device harness does not inject `monotonic`, so in tests/github-signin.test.ts a hold now runs on real `performance.now()` while `now`/`sleep` run on the injected clock: advancing `h.clock.t` there can never end a hold, and a hold set in that file is active for 30 s of wall time whatever the test clock says. Nothing fails today (device 56/56) because the only device case touching a hold, 11b (:549), expects the hold to be cleared by the commit, not by time, but a future device test that steps the clock past a hold would be wrong silently, and the two U5 harnesses now model different clocks for the same dependency.
findings.evidence: tests/github-signin.test.ts:140-142: `new GitHubSignIn({ store, vault, epoch: ..., fetcher: ..., config, now: clock.now, sleep: clock.sleep, limits: ... })` with no `monotonic`; its Clock (:63-75) has no monotonic reading. src/main/github-signin.ts:132 defaults it to `performance.now()`. tests/github-signin-refresh.test.ts:146-148 injects `monotonic: clock.monotonic`. grep 'renewalHeld: true|hold' in the device file: only 11b (:549-554) relies on a hold, and it asserts `renewalHeld: false` right after the commit, which commitPoint's `this.hold = null` (:310) gives regardless of the clock.
findings.fix: Give the device Clock the same `monotonic` reading and `step()` as the refresh Clock (or a shared helper) and pass `monotonic: clock.monotonic` in the device harness, tests only, no src change; or add one comment at the device harness saying holds there run on real time and no device case may time one out.
